Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 2 Player 4 Game End Overview The game is played over 2 rounds, each consisting of 11 turns Score the animals you collected at the end, but remember some animals score negatively Turn The player with the starting player token, plays a card, followed by the others The highest Unique card wins UNLESS There are duplicate cards. Of the players who played one of those duplicates, the one with the most pigs wins. If tied, the one that played the card first wins If there are different duplicate card sets, first the duplicate card there is the most of will be judged as above, then if still tied the duplicate group with the highest value will be judged as above Regardless of how you win, you gain the starting player token along with two animal cards played this turn of your choice. After which, in the new turn order, the other players pick from the remaining cards played to keep. This means whoever is in last turn order gets no card. For the first turn, BGA randomly allocates one of the players the starting player token 2 Player There is a Dummy The Dummy cannot win a turn As such, the purpose of the Dummy is to provide the chance of a duplicate card for either player to win via that method The Dummy always plays last and plays a randomly selected card from its hand Game End After everyone has played their entire hand once, deal a new hand to everyone After everyone has played their second hand, the game ends. Rabbits - 1-5 score, 6+ lose 5pts Bear - only pairs score, solos score nothing Giraffes - each giraffe scores by itself Owl - An owl scores nothing, but if you can pair it with a giraffe it scores Cat - Cats are multiplied by each other, e.g. 3 cats is 3x3 for 9 Fox - Foxes only lose points! Lions - having no or too few Lions lose points, have to have at least 2 to breakeven Pigs - have no score, but give tiebreaking when duplicates are played during a turn Pandas - most and least gain and lose points respectively Monkey - Wild for Rabbit, Bear, Giraffe, Owl, or Cat (during play its worth is one higher than the previous card played) The player with the highest score, wins! He slept! He slept! The king of the jungle fell asleep!
The news echoed throughout the forest that the lion was in a deep sleep, and now, the animals were in an uproar to find a new king, someone who had an air of nobility capable of pleasing mother nature and reigning with authority.
Then, the monkey asks the others: ‘Why don’t we choose Panda and make him King?’

Panda Rei is divided into 2 rounds, each one with 11 turns of card competition between players.

In each turn, players will play cards from their hands on the table trying to win to have the preference in choosing the cards played to be placed in front of them to be scored at the end of the game.

Normally, to win a dispute, the player must have played the card with the highest value on the table, however, if there is more than one equal card on the table, the card from the largest group repeated on the table with the highest value is what will win the dispute.

The winner of the dispute will receive 2 cards from those played on the table and will be the first to choose from those available, following the order of receipt and choice of cards for the players to the left of the winner of the dispute. This way, the last player (the one to the right of the person who won the dispute) will not receive a card in the turn.

At the end of two rounds, players will check the cards in front of them and count the points. The player with the most points is the winner!

—description from the designer

[Rating: 4/10] Played on BGA.  Cute animals, set collecting where card playing is crap shoot, but set collecting is obvious as to the optimal choice.

[Rating: 4.5/10] Only played with 2 players and it will play better with more players. I still feel like the Pig cards are too strong for breaking all ties. Ultimately, it will play better with more players but it is unlikely to hit the table again.

[Rating: 5/10] A trick taking card game where players are playing cards and the number of cards followed by highest number played by a player draws 2 cards and following player draws only 1 card. The last player will not collect any cards. Each animal card (each with a different value) having different set collection scoring. There's only 2 rounds and the player with the most points wins.

[Rating: 5/10] After 1 game on BGA: I like the cards, and I enjoy games with an animal theme. The bright, vibrant colors are refreshing. I also like that in each round (almost) every player gets something. From reading the rules, the two-player experience seems less than ideal, though I haven’t tried it yet. I find the mix of trick-taking and set collection creative.  What I don’t like: the card effects and the rules for winning a trick aren’t entirely intuitive.
